definitions.explanation: A place where trains or buses stop for passengers.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧。

examples.english: I'll get off at the next station.
There is a big shop in front of the station.
In the morning there are a lot of people at the station, so it's hard to get on the train.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{駅|えき}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{電車|でんしゃ}→電車：00522_densha⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{三|さん}→三：00749_san⟧つ⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{毎朝|まいあさ}→毎朝：00966_maiasa⟧⟦{同|おな}じ→同じ：02857_onaji⟧⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: My school is three stops from this station by train, so I leave home at the same time every morning.

notes:
{駅|えき} primarily refers to a train station. While it can technically include bus stations, in everyday usage it almost always means a railway station.

COMPOUNDS:
- ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧: area in front of the station (a common meeting spot)
- ⟦{駅員|えきいん}→駅員：05503_ekiin⟧: station staff
- ⟦{駅弁|えきべん}→駅弁：09702_ekiben⟧: boxed lunch sold at stations
- ⟦{終着駅|しゅうちゃくえき}→終着駅：23879_shuuchakueki⟧: terminal station
- ⟦{乗|の}り{換|か}え→乗り換え：16130_norikae⟧{駅|えき}: transfer station

USAGE:
Counting stations uses the counter つ⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧: ⟦{三|みっ}つ→三つ：02970_mittsu⟧⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{駅|えき} (the third station). When giving directions, Japanese speakers often measure distance in terms of how many stations away a place is.
